name: Acadia

colors.symbolism: the papal colour — the Church that sustained the Acadians

description: A French tricolor of blue, white and red with a golden five-pointed star in the upper hoist of the blue stripe.
history: Adopted at the Second Acadian National Convention at Miscouche, Prince Edward Island, on 15 August 1884. The tricolor marks the Acadians' French origins; the gold star is Stella Maris, Our Lady of the Assumption, patroness of the Acadians, placed in the papal colour.

features.symbolism: Our Lady of the Assumption, star of the sea, guiding the Acadian people
